title: A parcel service that never loses an order
summary: EnvíaYa delivers 80,000 parcels a day in the Bajío region. Each new order reaches billing, the customer SMS and driver assignment, and a failure in one does not stop the others.

requirements.1: {{s1}} sends the customer SMS by itself and delivers the same order-created event to other subscribers, without the API knowing how many there are.
requirements.2: {{s2}} receives its copy of each order and keeps it until a worker confirms it was processed; if the worker dies halfway, the order shows up again.
requirements.3: {{s3}} runs the code that assigns a driver only when there are messages, scales on its own and costs nothing in the early morning.
requirements.4: {{s4}} sets aside the order that fails 5 times so it can be reviewed later, so it is not retried forever.
requirements.5: {{s5}} receives the drivers' GPS, keeps it for 7 days in order, and analytics reads it again from the beginning as many times as it wants.

s1.explanation: When a message is published to a Notifications topic, the service sends it to all of the topic's subscriptions, including SMS and a function, at least once for each one. Queue is not a subscription protocol, so a function forwards the copy.
s1.hint_cue: sends the customer SMS by itself

s2.explanation: OCI Queue hides a delivered message for its visibility timeout and the consumer must delete it when done; if it is not deleted, the message can be delivered again to another consumer.
s2.hint_cue: if the worker dies halfway, the order shows up again

s3.explanation: A Connector Hub connector takes the messages from the queue, sends them to the function and then deletes them from the queue, so the code runs when there are messages. A Compute instance would stay on.

s4.explanation: If the function fails, the whole batch returns to the queue and each message adds a delivery; with 1-message batches in the connector, only the failing order reaches the maximum (1 to 20) and OCI Queue moves it to its DLQ. A bucket does not count deliveries.

s5.explanation: OCI Streaming delivers each partition's messages in order and does not delete them when read: analytics can replay them from any offset within the configured retention. Connector Hub only moves data.
s5.hint_cue: reads it again from the beginning

oci-cache.s2: OCI Cache is an in-memory cache: its lists do not guarantee delivery or bring the order back if the worker dies halfway.

oci-compute.s3: A Compute instance bills while it is running, even with no orders in the early morning, and it does not run on its own for each message.

oci-object-storage.s4: An Object Storage bucket stores objects, but it does not count a message's deliveries or set it aside on its own.
oci-object-storage.s5: Object Storage stores whole objects; it does not deliver positions in order per partition or with offsets to read them again.

oci-connector-hub.s3: Connector Hub moves the messages from the queue to a target, but it does not run the code that assigns a driver: that code lives in the target.
oci-connector-hub.s5: Connector Hub moves data from a source to a target and the source sets the retention; it does not keep the GPS to read it again.

oci-streaming.s1: In Streaming, consumers read messages from partitions by offset; delivering to subscriptions over SMS is what a Notifications topic does.
